head: working-tree
subject: MQTT broker cached event-loop timestamps in publish and QoS2 release paths
change: The broker's publish, bridge staging and QoS2 release paths now use netz_runtime.cachedAwakeNow instead of direct std.Io.Clock.awake.now calls. This reuses the executor's per-loop timestamp for the hot serial QoS2 path instead of issuing a fresh clock syscall for every publish/release transition.

benchmark.command: MQTT_QOS=2 PUBLISHERS=1 SUBSCRIBERS=1 MESSAGES=5000 PUBLISHER_WINDOW=1 MQTT_SESSION_EXPIRY_SECONDS=3600 zig build compare-mqtt-mosquitto
benchmark.workload: MQTT 5 over TCP, QoS 2, one publisher, one subscriber, 256-byte payload, persistent session
benchmark.observation: Netz serial QoS2 p50 fell from 73-95 us to 44-45 us and throughput rose from 9.3-11.4k to 16.0-17.1k publishes/s. The paired share of Mosquitto rose from roughly 0.48-0.52 to 0.60-0.63 under the same host-load band. The remaining gap is still dominated by task wakeups and parking.

full_library.notes: Earlier full runs under host load 10-42 failed only timing-sensitive HTTP/2 and WebSocket handshake-budget cases (and one SOCKS5 test-only socket close crash); each passed in isolation, and the final run at load 5-13 passed with no failures.

notes: The benchmark client is the same netz client for both brokers. Host load varied between runs; the A/B baseline was rerun immediately before the cached version under the same load band.
